analyzed_vuln.description: `xmlRemoveID` passes `attr->id->value` directly to `xmlHashRemoveEntry(...)`. The hash removal callback (`xmlFreeIDTableEntry` -> `xmlFreeID`) frees the same `xmlID` object that owns `attr->id->value`. After `xmlHashRemoveEntry` returns, `xmlRemoveID` still accesses `attr->id` (`attr->id = NULL` after checking/using it), causing a use-after-free on the just-freed `xmlID`/value pointer. Root cause is unsafe use of `attr->id` data as both lookup key and object being freed during removal, without preserving key or nulling state before free.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered when parsing XML that creates an ID attribute entry (via DTD/ATTLIST ID and element attributes) and then frees the corresponding attribute/node during parsing cleanup (e.g., entity expansion/content teardown in xml reader path). In the xml fuzz harness, attacker-controlled input defines ID attributes and causes node/prop destruction, leading `xmlFreeProp` to call `xmlRemoveID` on an ID-typed attribute. If the ID table entry matches that attribute, `xmlHashRemoveEntry` frees the `xmlID` while `xmlRemoveID` is still using fields derived from `attr->id`, producing UAF.
